Case for higher: the numerator is Medicare Part D only, so it understates an all-payer capture; and Kerendia's starts concentrate in this row's pool, since 1,445 of 2,680 FINE-REAL participants with a baseline value had UACR of 300 mg/g or more (54%, FINE-REAL interim, ASN 2025 presentation) against 17.9% of the CKD pool (7.8 / 43.5, Bailey 2014), so its capture here is higher than the whole-pool rate carried.
